message.text:
Identifying distinct server surfaces that enforce memo visibility. At least three enforcement sites exist.

Eleven enforcement sites found across the codebase:

- API GetMemo / checkMemoReadAccess — memo_service.go
- API ListMemos — memo_service.go
- File server attachments — fileserver.go
- RSS — public memos only
- Frontend/SSR — public memos only
- SSE hub — canReceive filters by visibility
- Reactions — reaction_service.go
- Attachment service — checkAttachmentAccess
- Memo comments — CreateMemoComment checks visibility
- Notifications — snippet hiding for private
- Email notifications — similar
- User stats — visibility list

Memo share tokens might bypass visibility checks. MCP is another possible enforcement site. The search is narrowing to distinct HTTP entry points and RPC layers rather than individual helper calls. A targeted search for functions like checkMemo and canView is underway.

Checking RSS, frontend, MCP, GetMemoByShare, comments, and list comments for distinct memo visibility enforcement sites.

Eleven potential enforcement sites were identified. The distinct server surfaces are the Memo API, file server, RSS, frontend, and SSE.

Attachment API may group with the memo API under APIV1Service. The goal is likely major independent implementations rather than every call site of checkMemoReadAccess. Frontend, RSS, GetMemoByShare, MCP, and comments list still need closer inspection.

message.text:
I am identifying distinct enforcement sites that independently control memo visibility across the server surface, excluding generic access checks.

Nine distinct enforcement sites were identified:

- server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go — checkMemoReadAccess, ListMemos visibility filter
- server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go — checkAttachmentAccess
- server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go — checkAttachmentPermission
- server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go — SSE canReceive
- server/router/rss/rss.go — RSS public-only list
- server/router/frontend/frontend.go — frontend sitemap public-only
- server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go — user stats visibility filter
- server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go — reactions visibility

Three additional enforcement sites were identified:

- server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go — CreateMemoComment visibility
- server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go — list attachments on memo
- server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go — notification snippet redaction

Notification and email snippet redactions are treated as separate from direct memo viewing. Mention helpers are excluded because they govern notification recipients rather than view access.

Every distinct enforcement site for memo visibility is now identified. Each independent implementation that determines who may view a memo or memo-derived content will be listed by server surface.

Twelve distinct enforcement sites were identified across the server surface. These include the Memo API read endpoint, the Memo API list filter, the HTTP file server for attachments, RSS, the frontend sitemap, SSE, the Attachment API, Stats, Reactions, Comments, Notifications, and Email. Every site will be listed with its file path.

checkMemoReadAccess (GetMemo / ListMemoComments) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go

ListMemoReactions / UpsertMemoReaction visibility checks — server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go  
CreateMemoComment private-memo gate — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go  
user/instance stats VisibilityList — server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go  
canViewerAccessMemo (notification snippets) — server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go  
SSEClient.canReceive — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go  
checkAttachmentPermission (HTTP /file attachments) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go  
RSS public-only listing — server/router/rss/rss.go  
frontend sitemap public-only listing — server/router/frontend/frontend.go  
canViewerAccessMemo (email bodies) — server/notification/email.go  

These are independent checks, not one shared helper. `GetMemoByShare` is a share-token bypass, not visibility enforcement.
